purpose: Perform the first physical-composition test demanded by v7.9. Take two copies of the smooth four-C4 twisted rigid transducer. Keep terminal 0 of the first copy and terminal 1 of the second copy open. Saturate the three dangling Hamiltonian vertices of the inner terminal 1 of copy A against the three dangling vertices of inner terminal 0 of copy B by one of the six perfect matchings. Track exact C4 orbit labels and gauges and test the actual three new vertex-colour inequalities. Prove that every one of the six physical splices destroys the 18-state permutation semantics and introduces a set-valued gain relation; the projected orbit relation simultaneously expands to the full 3x3 relation.

physical_splice_model.copy_A: Outer terminal A0 remains open; inner terminal A1 is F(A0).
physical_splice_model.copy_B: Inner terminal B0 is a free 18-state variable; outer terminal B1 is F(B0).
physical_splice_model.splice: Choose a bijection sigma of the three free ports {0,2,3}. Add Hamiltonian edges A1[p]--B0[sigma(p)] for p in {0,2,3}; every added edge requires unequal endpoint colours.
physical_splice_model.topology: Each source wire is three open Hamiltonian paths. A perfect matching of the three inner path endpoints joins the six paths into three longer open paths and creates no internal Hamiltonian cycle; the two outer terminals retain three dangling half-edges each.
physical_splice_model.boundary: The exact outer relation is recorded both on full states Omega x Omega, |Omega|=18, and on quotient triples (tau_left,tau_right,h_right^{-1}h_left) modulo global colour symmetry.

small_branching_control.meaning: One exact input state already has four legal output states after a single physical splice, so the loss of functionality is explicit and not an artifact of quotienting by global colour symmetry.

representative_14_triple_gain_profile.observation: The four pairs inside the {0,1}x{0,1} sector retain singleton gain transport, while every pair involving orbit 2 branches to two gains. The orbit relation itself is nevertheless universal.

main_theorem.name: PHYSICAL_THREE_EDGE_SPLICE_BREAKS_THE_RIGID_ORDER6_TRANSDUCER
main_theorem.statement: For all six perfect matchings of the three dangling inner-terminal ports of two v7.9 wires, the exact outer full-state relation is nonfunctional and the terminal orbit projection is the complete nine-pair relation. Four matchings yield 84 full-state pairs / 14 orbit-gain triples and two yield 132 / 22. Therefore the clean order-six permutation backbone of an abstract wire network does not survive even the first physical Hamiltonian splice operation.
proof: Use the exact v7.9 permutation F to determine A1 uniquely from each outer state A0 and B1 uniquely from each chosen inner state B0.
For each of the six bijections sigma on ports {0,2,3}, exhaust the 18 choices of A0 and 18 choices of B0 and retain exactly the pairs satisfying the three concrete splice inequalities.
Map every retained pair to the outer pair (A0,B1). No matching has one output per input: row cardinalities are {4,6} in four cases and {6,8} in two cases.

Quotient only after the full-state test. Every matching accepts all nine terminal orbit pairs. Refining by relative gain gives exactly 14 or 22 quotient triples, and multiplying by the six global colour gauges reproduces the full-state counts 84 or 132.

positive: Localizes the first genuine branching point sharply: it is not hidden inside one twisted wire, but is created by the physical NEQ splice between two otherwise rigid transducers.
Reduces the next residual language to two small exact set-valued gain atoms of sizes 14 and 22 rather than a generic 18-state relation.
Shows that orbit labels alone are useless after the splice; all remaining information lives in restricted relative S3 gain sets.
killed: Replace physical Hamiltonian splicing by abstract identification of complete terminal states and claim the order-six F-potential algorithm solves the composed source.
Assume the v7.9 rigid gain property is closed under joining its three dangling Hamiltonian vertices to another copy.
Track only the twisted orbit permutation after one physical splice; the orbit projection has already become universal.
firewall: The two-copy object is still source-open. Existence of a final relation-preserving completion to one smooth Hamiltonian cycle is not proved here.
The six matchings are exhaustive only for joining all three free ports of one designated inner terminal to all three free ports of the other designated inner terminal.
Set-valued gain branching does not by itself imply hardness; the 14/22 relations may still have a polynomial closure.
No SAT algorithm and no P=NP conclusion follows.

next_target.name: E8_S3_GAINSET_14_22_CLOSURE_V8_1
next_target.directive: Forget orbit-only reasoning for this branch. Treat the two exact quotient relations of sizes 14 and 22 as S3 gain-set constraints over the nine orbit pairs. Compute their relational closure under path composition, reversal and cycle holonomy while retaining source-open port interfaces. Determine whether the language collapses to a bounded permutation/coset system with polynomial propagation, or whether a small composition realizes a genuinely hard three-state/gain relation. Mandatory controls are the four-output branching witness above, the v7.9 order-six transducer, and the v7.8 three-wire gain-only relations.
